name: potala-palace

primary_references.authors: Wu et al. (2026), Built Heritage10:23; includes Potala Palace Management Office
primary_references.evidence: Field study identifies splashed kaolinite-based white finishing and iron-rich red earth; thick gravity-flow accumulations50–100mm. Figure1 is a front photograph; Figure3 supplies south/north facade color-elevation drawings. White frontage has mostly blank battered lower walls with two main upper window rows, broad dark parapets; central Red Palace has a vertical balcony band.
Describes a concave central balcony belt, dark brown upper band, contrasting white band, gilded copper plates, and a largely blank lower20m wall.

implementation: Potala-specific facade builder retains existing block footprints/heights and seven golden pavilions. Battered earthen-plaster faces, top-concentrated white window ranks, dark trapezoidal surrounds, timber lintel hoods, measured-scale plaster flow relief, dark tamarisk bands, white band beneath, copper plates, and a real central balcony recess replace generic full-height window arrays. Small blind warehouse apertures form two subordinate rows beneath the main window ranks, as documented by ChinaCulture and visible in the conservation elevation.
approximation_bounds: Individual window pitch/heights,2.2m balcony recess,1.7–3m upper bands and maximum3.5m wall batter are proportional facade estimates, not a measured architectural survey. Overall published117.2m roof height and mapped registry anchor remain unchanged. Finish relief is kept45mm while physical121 atlas supplies fine uneven texture.

terrain_evidence.correction: Extend first southwest lower-only cut11m west and7m north;18m feather replaces4m. Cut remains bounded around authored foundation and lower-only, with surrounding Marpo Ri preserved.

engine_review_status: Source consumer encodes validated; central rebake and production-engine confirmation still required.
